skills.trigger: When evaluating cystic lung disease on chest imaging to distinguish bronchiectasis from other cystic pathologies like LAM or PLCH.
steps: Inspect the cyst walls for thickness; identify if they are thick-walled versus thin-walled.
Check for the presence of air-fluid levels within the cystic spaces, which indicate retained secretions.
Assess the distribution pattern; note if cysts are clustered (often lower/mid-zone) rather than diffuse and uniform.
Differentiate from Lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM), which presents with thin-walled, round cysts evenly distributed without air-fluid levels.
Differentiate from Pulmonary Langerhans' Cell Histiocytosis (PLCH), which typically shows bizarre-shaped cysts and nodules with upper-lobe predominance and costophrenic angle sparing.
